title: What's new in Framewise 0.6
notes: A brand-new look: the Pro Camera design. Your camera picture now fills the whole screen, like a real viewfinder.
New tabs at the bottom: Live, Coach, History and Setup. Everything is one tap away.
Fresh Electric Cyan colours and our new slogan: "Frame it. Tune it. Own it."
The Coach screen shows a score for your shot and clear tips: what your setting is now and what to try instead.
Shutter, aperture, ISO, EV and white balance are shown in one strip under the picture.
Fonts are now built into the app, so it looks the same everywhere, even without internet.
A brand-new look: the Pro Camera design. Your camera picture now fills the whole screen, like a real viewfinder.
New tabs at the bottom: Live, Coach, History and Setup. Everything is one tap away.
Fresh Electric Cyan colours and our new slogan: "Frame it. Tune it. Own it."
The Coach screen shows a score for your shot and clear tips: what your setting is now and what to try instead.
Shutter, aperture, ISO, EV and white balance are shown in one strip under the picture.
Fonts are now built into the app, so it looks the same everywhere, even without internet.
Test reports now go straight to the Framewise developer. Tap "Send test report" (or "Yes, send" after a crash) and you'll see "Sent, thanks!".
No internet? The report waits and is sent automatically the next time Framewise opens.
Prefer email or WhatsApp? Use "Share another way".
Your API key, passwords and photos are still never included. Reports are deleted after 90 days.
Fixed: "Could not reach GitHub" errors when checking for updates. Framewise now uses a lighter update check that GitHub doesn't limit.
Tapping "Check for updates" many times in a row no longer causes errors. If GitHub is busy, Framewise waits and tries again later.
Clearer messages: the camera Wi-Fi tip only shows when your phone is actually on the camera's Wi-Fi.
Test reports are tidier: each update error is logged once, and closing the app no longer logs a USB disconnect.
Fixed: after tapping a button, a lit-up outline stayed around it until you tapped somewhere else. Buttons now just flash briefly when you press them.
Hover effects now only apply with a mouse, so nothing stays lit on a touch screen.
Fixed: the camera name in the top right now shows the camera you picked (Canon or Sony) instead of always saying Sony.
Setup → Live view now starts with a camera picker: Sony a6100 or Canon 2000D. You only see the steps for your camera.
Then pick how you connect. Sony: Wi-Fi or USB-C. Canon: USB-C or Wi-Fi (experimental). Framewise remembers your choice.
When a camera connects, Framewise selects it for you.
The copyright line moved to the bottom of the app, as small text under the Framewise name. It's still in Setup → About.
New: connect with a USB-C cable to a Sony a6100 or Canon EOS 2000D. This is experimental and not tested on a real camera yet.
New: Canon EOS 2000D live view over the camera's own Wi-Fi. Also experimental and untested. The steps are in Setup → Live view.
Pick your connection in Setup → Live view: Sony Wi-Fi, USB-C cable or Canon Wi-Fi. Unplug and replug the cable and Framewise reconnects.
New Report tab: tap Send test report to share what happened through email, WhatsApp or any app. Your API key and passwords are never included.
After a crash or error, Framewise offers to send a report the next time it opens. You can switch this off.
Fixed: the "update available" message shows up by itself again when you open Framewise or come back to it.
New About tab with credits. © 2026 errevsPhotography. All rights reserved.
Reconnecting to the camera right after disconnecting is faster and more reliable.
Tapping "Check for updates" and "Install update" quickly no longer starts two downloads at once.
The History screen can no longer break because of an old or damaged saved entry.
Your shot history still stays on your phone only.
New History tab (Setup → History): every shot you analyse is saved with its camera settings and the AI tips.
Each AI reading now also gives your shot a score from 1 to 10.
Tips get more personal: Framewise tells the AI about your last 20 shots, like your usual settings and problems that keep coming back.
Your history stays on your phone. It is never uploaded on its own; only a short summary goes along with an AI request you start.
Tap Clear history at any time to delete it all.
Cleaned up: the old "share the Sony app's screen" option is gone. It kept disconnecting, and the direct Wi-Fi live view works much better.
Framewise no longer asks for screen sharing, notification or "display over other apps" permissions.
Live view over the camera's own Wi-Fi works exactly as before.
A USB-C cable connection is on the way in 0.4 as a backup option.
Live view now connects straight to your camera over its own Wi-Fi. You no longer need the Sony app.
Framewise reads your shutter speed, aperture and ISO from the camera and fills them in for you.
AI suggestions keep using your mobile data while you're connected to the camera.
The Sony app option is still there, but it disconnects as soon as you switch away from it, so the direct connection is the better choice.
You'll now see these "What's new" notes before you update, and once after the update.
Framewise can now update itself. It tells you when a new version is ready, and you install it with one tap.
Clearer messages while you connect live view, so you can see what's happening at each step.
A small floating Framewise button helps you jump back to the app.
Updates are checked for safety before they install.
